summary: Backend-only verification of the Emergent email proxy -> direct Resend REST API swap. All 7 pytest cases pass. Module-level: email_service.is_configured() returns True with the newly-set RESEND_API_KEY / RESEND_FROM_EMAIL / EMAIL_FROM_NAME env vars; _from_header() returns 'Burger Times <orders@burgertimes.fr>'; the module is a proper no-op when RESEND_API_KEY is missing (verified in a clean subprocess). End-to-end: POST /api/checkout/session with customer_email=delivered@resend.dev returned 200 with order_id/order_number, and backend logs show `POST https://api.resend.com/emails HTTP/1.1 200 OK` followed by `INFO:email_service:Resend email sent to delivered@resend.dev (subject='Commande confirmée · #BT-...')`. Telegram sidecar still works: `POST https://api.telegram.org/bot.../sendMessage HTTP/1.1 200 OK` fired in the same request. Admin status update to 'accepted' triggered a second Resend send (subject 'Commande acceptée'). No new calls to integrations.emergentagent.com after the swap. /api/menu still returns 40 items and /api/categories 9, admin login still works.

test_results.email_service_noop_when_unset: PASS - subprocess with RESEND_API_KEY unset: is_configured=False and send_order_email(...) returns without raising.
test_results.checkout_session_triggers_resend_and_tel: PASS - order BT-A6PP46 created (order_id returned), backend log shows POST https://api.resend.com/emails 200 OK + 'Resend email sent to delivered@resend.dev (subject="Commande confirmée · #BT-A6PP46")' + POST https://api.telegram.org/bot.../sendMessage 200 OK. No integrations.emergentagent.com hits.
test_results.admin_status_accepted_triggers_email: PASS - PUT /api/admin/orders/{id}/status {status:'accepted'} produced a second POST api.resend.com/emails 200 OK, subject 'Commande acceptée · #BT-A6PP46'.
test_results.cleanup_delete_order: PASS - test order deleted via DELETE /api/admin/orders/{id}.

critical_code_review_comments: email_service._post_email logs subject at INFO but not the Resend message id from the response body — logging r.json().get('id') would make prod tracing easier when correlating with the Resend dashboard.

send_order_email is awaited synchronously in POST /api/checkout/session under a try/except; Resend p99 latency is ~800ms, so a slow Resend call will delay the checkout HTTP response by up to 30s (httpx timeout). Consider asyncio.create_task(...) for true fire-and-forget, matching the Telegram pattern which is already inline but wraps update logic separately.
No retry on 5xx from Resend. A single transient upstream error will lose the confirmation email silently (only a WARNING log). Acceptable for MVP but worth a followup.
